references.text: Paul emphasizes the same principle: "What do you have that you did not receive?" Everything we have is given to us by God, which aligns with the Baptist's words that a person cannot take anything unless it has been given from heaven ([ref:1 Cor 4:7|1 Corinthians 4:7]).
James confirms that "every good and perfect gift comes from above, from the Father of lights." This supports John's statement that everything is given from heaven ([ref:Jas 1:17|James 1:17]).
Jesus says to Pilate: "You would have no power over me if it had not been given to you from above." The same principle that all authority and gifts come from heaven ([ref:John 19:11|John 19:11]).
Jesus says that no one can come to him unless it is given to them by the Father. This reflects the Baptist's recognition that everything is given from heaven ([ref:John 6:65|John 6:65]).

"No one takes this honor upon himself, but he is called by God." No one can take on a ministry unless it is given to them by God – the same principle expressed by the Baptist ([ref:Heb 5:4|Hebrews 5:4]).

Shortly after in the same conversation, the Baptist states that "the one who comes from above is over all." This expands on his recognition that Christ's ministry is given from heaven and therefore surpasses his own ([ref:John 3:31|John 3:31]).

David confesses that everything comes from God: "From you comes everything, and of what we have received from your hand, we have given to you." This shows the Old Testament foundation for the Baptist's statement ([ref:1 Chr 29:14|1 Chronicles 29:14]).

The Father loves the Son and has given all things into his hands. This confirms that Jesus' ministry and authority are given to him from heaven, which the Baptist just acknowledged ([ref:John 3:35|John 3:35]).

Paul urges everyone not to think more highly of themselves than they ought, but to think soberly "according to the measure of faith that God has assigned to each." All service is given as a gift from God ([ref:Rom 12:3|Romans 12:3]).
